item.title: US Supreme Court again rejects Trump's bid to overturn $5mn E Jean Carroll verdict
item.description: The US Supreme Court again rejected Donald Trump's attempt to overturn a civil verdict. A jury had previously found him liable for sexual abuse and defamation against E. Jean Carroll. This decision leaves a $5 million judgment in place, which Trump has now paid. Another separate $83.3 million verdict against Trump is still pending before the Supreme Court.

item.title: Only talks can resolve issues, hope Bangladesh PM visits India soon: Trivedi
item.description: Indian High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi stressed dialogue for resolving bilateral issues between India and Bangladesh. He expressed hope that Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's visit to India should occur much sooner. Bangladesh government attached tough conditions for New Delhi prior to the possible bilateral visit. An Indian business delegation began a three-day visit to strengthen economic engagement. Both nations share a dream and acknowledge inherent challenges within democracy.
item.dc:creator: Ahsan Tasnim

item.title: Meta goes to trial this week, which, if it loses, could change Insta & FB forever
item.description: Meta has been hit with a major lawsuit regarding child safety and the addictive nature of its platform. Various states are demanding significant financial compensation and operational reforms, arguing that Meta intentionally crafted features to be addictive for young users. Additionally, they allege that the company collects data from children under the age of thirteen without obtaining proper consent.

item.title: Streamer Pool Incident Debate: Sara Saffari confronts Rawdogmoon; $40,000 Rolex sparks X backlash
item.description: Sara Saffari confronted Twitch streamer Rawdogmoon after he threw her into a pool at Cinna’s party while she was wearing a reported $40,000 Rolex. She appeared angry and questioned his decision. Another clip showed Saffari asking about an alleged E-date involving Sophie Rain. The videos sparked mixed reactions online, with viewers discussing both incidents and the watch.

item.title: Meet Mohammed Almuntasir: Libyan photographer's video proves "ghost cat" still lives
item.description: In a groundbreaking 2017 video, a Libyan photographer captured the elusive sand cats, marking the first sighting of these fascinating creatures in their natural habitat. This revelation sparked an extensive eight-year research collaboration between zoologist Firas Hayder and photographer Mohammed Almuntasir, who combined their expertise and local insights to gather essential data. Their ongoing efforts are instrumental in enhancing our understanding of sand cat populations in Libya.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 1745, the US welcomed mimosa trees for pink flowers; they later spread invasively
item.description: Mimosa, introduced to the United States around 1745, quickly became a sought-after ornamental tree. However, it broke free from cultivation, proliferating in disturbed environments throughout the southern and eastern U.S. Its rapid growth and abundance of seeds have turned it into an invasive species, vying with native flora and reshaping ecosystems. Effective management must focus on both current plants and their future offspring to mitigate this ongoing issue.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: After 19 years, a beaver returned to a California creek, reshaping its habitat
item.description: Following a devastating fire in 2016 that impacted Strawberry Creek, Great Basin National Park staff noticed signs of beaver activity prompting restoration initiatives in 2021. By constructing artificial dams, the project significantly enhanced the creek's ecosystem and led to a remarkable increase in trout populations. In 2024, a beaver was spotted for the first time in nearly two decades, symbolizing nature's resilience and recovery after human efforts.

item.title: David and Victoria Beckham win battle for 'Blackpool-style' lights at £6.15m Cotswolds home
item.description: David and Victoria Beckham have won permission for ‘Blackpool-style’ lake illuminations, a hot tub and firepit at their £6.15 million Cotswolds home, despite objections from a critic living in Australia. The planning approval comes with conditions, including a ban on motorised boats and restrictions on firepit use during bird-nesting season at the estate.

item.title: 30 lions and tigers leave notorious Argentine zoo; head to new sanctuaries
item.description: Thirty lions and tigers from Argentina’s shuttered Lujan Zoo have begun a major relocation to wildlife sanctuaries in South Africa and the US. Led by Four Paws, the rescue involves moving 30 big cats that spent years in cramped cages and suffered health problems. The animals will now travel to Lionsrock in South Africa and The Wild Animal Sanctuary in Colorado.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Only nine such butterflies were found in US in 2022; 3 years later, over 1,300 were released
item.description: Researchers in Michigan have helped bring the Poweshiek skipperling butterfly back from the brink of extinction after its US wild population fell to just nine in 2022. Through captive breeding, habitat restoration and carefully planned releases, more than 1,300 butterflies were released in 2025. The recovery effort has now expanded to other endangered butterflies, while restored prairie habitats are helping support wider ecosystems.
